p_titre: Evaluating the reliability of highly demanding Power Electronic for electrical mobility : key findings from Archimedes Chips JU Project & other collaborative projects
p_liste_auteurs: Marina Labalette
pf_titre: Evaluating the reliability of highly demanding Power Electronic for electrical mobility : key findings from Archimedes Chips JU Project & other collaborative projects
pf_notes:
To achieve carbon neutrality by 2050, the EU Green Deal outlines a range of initiatives, including the development of efficient, safe, and environmentally friendly transportation systems. A key element of this strategy is the large-scale electrification of vehicles, including planes, cars, and trains.
Wide Band Gap (WBG) components, based on SiC (Silicon Carbide) and GaN (Gallium Nitride) technologies, are promising candidates to support this rapid electrification. However, ensuring their reliability is a critical prerequisite. This is the main focus of the Archimedes Chips Joint Undertaking (JU) project, which aims to develop reliable, dependable, and robust WBG technologies.
In this talk, the speaker will share insights into the Archimedes project, as well as highlight other collaborative initiatives at IRT, such as SiCRET and GaNRET. Finally, the conclusion will address the potential unintended consequences of relying solely on electrification measures, involving massive use of Power Electronics, to achieve decarbonization.”
